static_traits.name: Li Dean
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with friends are affected by persistent self-criticism; has a few friends to talk to, but has not yet discussed negative thoughts about drumming with them
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; has not yet received psychotherapy before; no similar psychological problems in the past
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative, neutral tone; capable of self-reflection but tending toward harsh self-criticism

basic_info.main_problem: I often have negative thoughts about my drumming ability, leading to feelings of powerlessness and discouragement.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these negative thoughts about my drumming ability have affected my passion for music and my overall mood.
growth_experiences: A few months ago I made mistakes drumming in a high-pressure performance before a large audience; since then, every practice or performance brings recurring negative automatic thoughts like 'I am terrible' and 'I will fail again', with tension and anxiety, more mistakes, and difficulty enjoying drumming; I try to cope by doubling practice and seeking comfort from friends, but positive feedback is hard to accept, the negative thoughts keep intensifying, spilling into daily mood and interactions with friends.

special_situations.event: A drumming mistake during a performance in front of a large audience a few months ago
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make mistakes in performance, it means I am incompetent / terrible
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling practice and seeking comfort from friends to prove myself, easing anxiety

special_situations.event: Each time I practice or prepare for a performance, recalling that mistake causes stress and tension to rise
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I must be perfect to be qualified; any error means failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly increasing practice time to avoid mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am going to mess up again

special_situations.event: When friends give positive feedback or comfort
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others' positive evaluations are not trustworthy; only making no mistakes can prove I am not bad
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Seeking external approval on one hand, negating positive feedback on the other
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are just saying nice things; actually I am terrible

special_situations.event: Last week, when rehearsing for a small performance, made frequent mistakes in simple sections
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Past failures predict future failures; I always make mistakes on stage
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Pushing through practice amid anxiety, ignoring objective evaluation of performance
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I make another mistake, the consequences will be terrible

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as a competent drummer and to enjoy music again
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failing again and being negated by audiences or friends, losing confidence and passion
defense_goal: Preventing mistakes and shame through self-criticism
Buffering anxiety through high-intensity practice and seeking comfort, maintaining a sense of control

object_relations.object_representation: Others/friends who don't understand me and only offer superficial comfort

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When others (friends or the counselor) give positive feedback or comfort
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to think others act only out of kindness or don't truly understand me (transference: projecting inner doubts onto others' motives)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Downplaying positive feedback, emphasizing one's own inadequacy; tone is restrained but firm, repeating the self-evaluation 'I am actually terrible' to maintain existing beliefs.

manifestations: Negative thinking makes drumming no longer enjoyable, passion declining
Devotion to music swallowed up by repeated expectations of failure
Not yet discussed negative thoughts with friends
outcomes: Available support not yet fully utilized

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Harshly fixating on mistakes during practice and globally negating
In interactions with friends, appears tense and reserved due to self-criticism

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Believing friends' comfort is only out of kindness, not genuine
Assuming others don't understand my real difficulties

positive_force: Maintaining stable performance in the work domain, showing resilience and self-efficacy
Has a few trustworthy friends who can provide support
Willing to try behavioral experiments of recording and objective analysis; has motivation to change
negative_force: Strong cognitive biases such as catastrophizing and overgeneralization
Harsh self-criticism and high sensitivity to mistakes cause anxiety and tension
Seeking external approval yet negating positive feedback, struggling to internalize positive information
High arousal under performance pressure heightens anticipation of failure

target_behavior.behavior: Intense self-criticism and anxiety when drumming, tension and frequent mistakes
antecedent: When performing in front of an audience or preparing to perform
Doubting and negating after receiving friends' positive feedback
target_behavior.core_reason: A core negative belief of 'I am terrible / will fail' and catastrophic expectations formed after one public performance mistake, triggering tension and anxiety in practice and performance
target_behavior.function: Escaping failure and shame (seeking control through self-criticism and increased practice), and temporarily easing anxiety by seeking comfort from others
target_behavior.consequence: Difficulty enjoying music and drumming, decreased practice efficiency with more mistakes, interpersonal tension, overall worse mood
